name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,487

clue.text: County side's opening game

indicators.note: one side of a word is one of its halves, so only half of the county's name is kept
an opening is where something begins, so only the first letter of that word is kept

blocks.note: the front half of Cheshire, an English county
first letter of side's

explanation.surface: A county sports team's first match of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County side' looks like a cricket team; read it as one side (half) of CHESHIRE, an English county in the north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game played between two players with kings, queens and pawns.

clue.text: Was able to dismiss unionist as indifferent

indicators.note: to dismiss something is to send it away, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: past tense of can
U is the abbreviation for Unionist

explanation.surface: Someone managed to sack a trade unionist because they did not care.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is unfeeling and unenthusiastic, showing no warmth or interest.

clue.text: Venus Williams finally overwhelmed by German veteran in Split

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
split means broken apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: last letter of Williams
G is the abbreviation for German
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Venus Williams loses to a seasoned German player in a match in Split, the Croatian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Venus looks like the tennis player's first name, but it is the definition; Split is the anagram signal, not the Croatian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet Venus appears brightly in the western sky after sunset, hence its traditional name.

clue.text: Warily reluctant to drink rum of poor quality

indicators.note: a drinker takes something inside, so the first word swallows the second

blocks.note: shy means wary and hesitant
rum is British slang for strange

explanation.surface: A cautious person hesitates to drink some rather nasty rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum reads as the spirit, but here it is the old British adjective meaning peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are badly made or inferior, cheap work done carelessly.

clue.text: Initially misleading Poor Tom with Lear's confused state

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts
poor means in bad condition, so the following letters are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: first letter of misleading
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: In King Lear, Edgar disguised as Poor Tom shares the storm with the mad king.
explanation.walkthrough: Poor Tom is Edgar's disguise in Shakespeare's King Lear, so 'Poor' seems part of a name; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, used figuratively for a scene of violent turmoil and chaos.

clue.text: Plain old declaration of intent

blocks.note: manifest means clear or obvious
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned, straightforward statement of what someone means to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a public statement of a party's or group's policies and aims.

clue.text: A struggle with English for fellow in crew

indicators.note: X for Y means X takes the place of Y, so one letter is swapped out for another

blocks.note: a fight is a struggle
E is the abbreviation for English
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: An Englishman standing in for a team-mate in a rowing crew has a battle on his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The English E replaces the fellow F at the front of the struggle word.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a racing rowing boat or its team of eight oarsmen, as in the Boat Race.

clue.text: Work gear brought up on line by quiet retail assistant

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up means reading it from bottom to top

blocks.note: sh is a call for quiet
OP is short for opus, a work
rig is equipment or gear
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A quiet shop worker carries work equipment up on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopgirl is an old term for a young woman who serves customers in a shop.

clue.text: It's difficult to get out of game against Thailand

definitions.text: It's difficult to get out of

blocks.note: RU is Rugby Union, a game
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A tough match against the Thai team that is hard to escape from.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a deep groove or a dull routine, both hard to climb out of once in it.

clue.text: Monty's first thoughts about a flower show on TV

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the name just before it

blocks.note: first letter of Monty's
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower
the mind is where thoughts are held

explanation.surface: Monty Don, the TV gardener, muses on a flower show broadcast on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here means concerning, tying the thoughts to the flower; the flower's letters come before the thoughts. Mastermind is a long-running BBC quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastermind is a BBC television quiz programme with its famous black chair and specialist subjects.

clue.text: Accept without protest and remain in adversity

blocks.note: to lie is to remain in a place, as in lie idle
down means in low spirits or fortune

explanation.surface: Advice to put up with hardship and endure it quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down under something, or take it lying down, is to submit meekly without resisting.

clue.text: Caves in over occupying the centre of Abbotsford following something very unpleasant

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this part goes behind the nasty thing
to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other
the centre means only the middle letters of the place name are used

blocks.note: grot is British slang for anything grubby or nasty
the two middle letters of Abbotsford
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Something nasty collapses at the heart of Abbotsford, Walter Scott's Scottish home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caves in' looks like collapses, but Caves is the definition. Abbotsford has ten letters, so its centre is the fifth and sixth.
explanation.definitionFit: Grottos are small caves, often picturesque or artificial ones in gardens.

clue.text: Untiring when debating life travelling round America

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so these letters move into a new order
round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go about the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A tireless debater argues about life on a tour of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefatigable describes someone who never gets weary, persisting tirelessly.

clue.text: Aggressive tendency to grab before taking a breather on the way up

indicators.note: grabbing something means holding it inside, so this word encloses the rest
in a down entry, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a bent is a natural inclination
a fish breathes through a gill
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A combative streak that grabs things before pausing for breath on a climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The before word takes the upturned breather in front of it, and the tendency word holds both.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerent means hostile and eager to fight, warlike in attitude.

clue.text: A variety of omens? Start worrying!

indicators.note: worrying means pulling about and shaking, as a dog does a bone, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sees a whole range of bad omens and begins to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start worrying!' reads as advice to begin fretting; Start is fodder, worrying the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a mixed collection of different kinds of things, such as chocolates in a box.

clue.text: Idle talk about head of engineering plant

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the talk word is read backwards
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: gas is empty chatter
first letter of engineering

explanation.surface: Pointless chatter about the chief of an engineering factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like a factory alongside engineering, but it means a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is a grey-leaved aromatic herb, a garden plant used in cooking.

clue.text: We object over having fish with fruit for sweet

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the pronoun is read backwards

blocks.note: us is the object form of we
the gar is a long-snouted fish
a plum is a fruit

explanation.surface: Diners complain about being served fish with fruit for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We object' looks like a protest; it means the grammatical object of we.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugarplum is a small round sweet of boiled sugar, famous from The Nutcracker.

clue.text: German book about packing fruit

indicators.note: packing something means stuffing it inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the others

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
re means concerning
to book a performer is to engage them

explanation.surface: A German book all about packing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The German and book pieces together pack the about piece between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a sweet green variety of plum, a fruit grown in orchards.

clue.text: Film oddly ignored pursuing charge admitted by London area leader of Hell's Angels

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the charge goes inside the other letters
the leader of a word is its first letter
ignoring the odd letters keeps just the even-numbered ones
pursuing means chasing behind, so this part comes at the end

blocks.note: SE is the south-east postcode district of London
a rap is a criminal charge
first letter of Hell's
the second and fourth letters of film

explanation.surface: A film about a London chapter of the Hell's Angels biker gang facing charges.
explanation.walkthrough: Hell's Angels reads as the biker gang, but Hell's only gives its first letter and Angels is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels, the plural of seraph.

clue.text: Win only against those without a goal? Not quite

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word goes around another
not quite means nearly but not exactly, so a close relative of the word is used in its place

blocks.note: on can mean against, as in an attack on
the near demonstrative, close to but not quite the far one
having no goal at all, a nil score

explanation.surface: A footballing jibe about a team that cannot score, betting only on a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose parse: 'Not quite' turns those into the near form these, which holds the no-goal piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet placed on the nose backs a horse to finish first only, with no each-way place element.

clue.text: Look for 'ROAD' in French

blocks.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written with a 1 that looks like I
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking what the French call a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, a crossword staple for road. The clue tempts you to translate road into French, but only in is translated.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's mien is their appearance or bearing, the look or manner they show.

clue.text: Writer includes an afterthought on current digestive aid

indicators.note: something that includes other things holds them inside it

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A writer adds a postscript about the latest stomach remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepsin is a stomach enzyme that breaks down proteins, sometimes taken to assist digestion.

clue.text: Deliberately disregard innately rude bishop's rambling

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Ignoring a naturally boorish bishop's long-winded sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn a blind eye is the idiom for knowingly pretending not to notice something wrong.

clue.text: Place to go to suppress tension before start of the game

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down inside, so the loo word encloses the next letters
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the loo is British slang for the toilet, where one goes
T is the symbol for tension in physics
first letter of the

explanation.surface: Nervous before kick-off, a player heads to the toilet to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place to go' is the toilet; loo is the British word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, also the name of a national lottery draw.

clue.text: Give way in the beginning by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase asks for a word that is heard the same as another one

blocks.note: a seed is the origin or start of something

explanation.surface: Someone seems to back down right at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to yield or surrender ground, power or territory to another.

clue.text: Within which one may be heard having a go on an organ

definitions.text: Within which one may be heard

blocks.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
a shot is a try or turn

explanation.surface: Someone takes a turn playing a church organ loudly enough to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ suggests the instrument in a church, but it is a body part; 'on' puts the go after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the range of hearing, so within earshot means close enough to be heard.

clue.text: Nonsense coming from revolutionary needing no introduction

indicators.note: no introduction means the first letter is taken away

blocks.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Rubbish spouted by a famous revolutionary everybody already knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' sounds like praise for a famous figure; it means losing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is informal for rubbish or foolish talk, as in talking rot.

clue.text: Extremely rare to have name removed from novelist's grave

indicators.note: extremely points to the two extremes, the outer letters of the word
removed from means a letter is taken out of the following word

blocks.note: Jane Austen, the novelist
N is the abbreviation for name
first and last letters of rare

explanation.surface: A rare event: a famous novelist's grave left without a name.
explanation.walkthrough: Grave looks like a burial place beside the novelist, but it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severe and stern in manner, which matches grave in the sense of solemn.

clue.text: Tribal symbol of tailless cat encountered on the way back by European

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off
going back means the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
met means encountered
a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: A docked cat met on a homeward walk alongside a European.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a carved post bearing tribal emblems, made by Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Explosive constituent found in container brought back by soldiers

indicators.note: brought back means turned the other way, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a tin is a container
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers return with a canister holding part of a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidising ingredient in gunpowder.
